nature-eecon-202.q: When does the UN project world population to peak, and at about what size?
nature-eecon-202.a: At about 10.3 billion in the mid-2080s, as of 2024.

nature-eecon-206.q: How much of the variation in income across countries did the growth model with human capital explain?

nature-eecon-185.q: What does overconsumption beyond the environment's long-term carrying capacity cause?
nature-eecon-185.a: Ecological overshoot, resource depletion and poorer ecosystem health.

nature-eecon-253.q: What is the Brandt Line, in the Global North and South divide?
nature-eecon-253.a: A line proposed by Willy Brandt in the 1980s that visualizes the divide at roughly 30 degrees North; it is criticized as outdated but still used to show global inequalities.

nature-eecon-152.q: Who coined the term green growth in 2005, and where did it first emerge?
nature-eecon-152.a: Rae Kwon Chung of UNESCAP coined it, and it first emerged at a ministerial conference in Seoul.

nature-eecon-165.q: What happened to US sulfur dioxide emissions between 1970 and 2006, while real GDP grew 195%?
nature-eecon-165.a: They fell from 31 million tons to 15 million.

nature-eecon-188.q: What is the aim of planned obsolescence in terms of sales?
nature-eecon-188.a: To boost long-term sales by shortening the time between repeat purchases, the 'replacement cycle'.

nature-eecon-167.q: In environmental policy, which two positions does agrowth oppose?

nature-eecon-254.q: What are some roots of the simple-living lifestyle?
nature-eecon-254.a: Buddhism, Taoism, Epicureanism and Thoreau's Walden (1854).

nature-eecon-141.q: In ecological economics, how do some economists treat the old classical factor 'land'?
nature-eecon-141.a: They widen it into natural capital within classical economics.

nature-eecon-182.q: What effect have educating and empowering women and giving access to family planning had on birthrates?
nature-eecon-182.a: A demonstrated effect of lowering them.

nature-eecon-153.q: Why can apparent decoupling of growth from environmental impact be misleading?
nature-eecon-153.a: It often comes from shifting environmental impact from high-consumption to low-consumption countries.

nature-eecon-189.a: Deliberately disabling a working product, such as ink cartridge chips that stop use while ink remains.

nature-eecon-184.q: What happened to total fuel consumption after the 1973 and 1979 oil crises, even though cars became more fuel-efficient?

nature-eecon-233.q: How much e-waste was generated globally in 2022, and how much of it was formally collected and recycled?
nature-eecon-233.a: About 62 million tonnes, only 22.3% of it formally collected and recycled.

nature-eecon-057.q: What is the goal of zero waste?
nature-eecon-057.a: To send nothing to landfills, incinerators, oceans or anywhere else in the environment.

nature-eecon-019.q: What two principles does material flow analysis rest on?
nature-eecon-019.a: A systems approach and mass balance, the conservation of matter.

nature-eecon-031.q: Under a flat rate or tax for waste collection, what incentive is there to reduce waste?
nature-eecon-031.a: None, because everyone pays the same.

nature-eecon-010.q: How much value added does the bioeconomy produce, according to the European Commission's science service?

nature-eecon-049.q: What obstacles create a 'repair monopoly' that right-to-repair rules target?
nature-eecon-049.a: Manufacturer-only servicing, restricted parts and tools, and software locks.

nature-eecon-234.q: What did the EU's RoHS Directive of 2003 target?
nature-eecon-234.a: Alternatives to hazardous materials such as cadmium, mercury and lead.

nature-eecon-235.q: How does ecological sanitation treat human excreta and wastewater?
nature-eecon-235.a: As a resource, hence the name resource-oriented sanitation, and it favors no single toilet technology.

nature-eecon-011.q: In the cascading use of biomass, what is finding the best pattern for a given biomass called?

nature-gov-129.q: What was the Khian Sea incident that helped trigger the Basel Convention?
nature-gov-129.a: A ship carrying Philadelphia incinerator ash dumped half its load on a beach in Haiti.

nature-gov-147.q: Who developed the concept of multilevel governance in the early 1990s?
nature-gov-147.a: Liesbet Hooghe and Gary Marks, from studying the structures the EU created under the 1992 Maastricht Treaty.

nature-gov-140.q: How is UNEP, which coordinates environmental responses within the UN, widely regarded?

nature-gov-158.q: What did 1970s research show about CFCs that led to the ozone treaties?
nature-gov-158.a: Man-made CFCs, used in products such as refrigerators, break down atmospheric ozone.

nature-gov-119.a: Top-down fisheries management often failed, and communities ignored rules, such as cuts in total allowable catch, that they did not understand.

nature-gov-157.q: Which event is seen as the beginning of international environmental law and policy?

nature-gov-161.q: When did the UNECE Water Convention on transboundary watercourses enter into force?
nature-gov-161.a: On 6 October 1996, after being signed in Helsinki in 1992.

nature-gov-046.q: How did the CBD change the treatment of genetic resources from earlier agreements?
nature-gov-046.a: Earlier agreements treated them as common heritage; the CBD gave each state sovereign rights over those in its territory.
